name: Chordoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and radiological diagnostic criteria for chordoma

criteria.description: Presence of physaliphorous cells with vacuolated cytoplasm on histology
MRI or CT showing destructive midline bone lesion with soft tissue mass in sacrococcygeal or clival region
Positive staining for brachyury, cytokeratin, and S100 protein
Symptoms consistent with local mass effect in typical anatomical locations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with physaliphorous cells plus characteristic imaging findings and positive brachyury immunostaining
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Brachyury immunostaining is considered a highly specific marker for chordoma.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive sacral or clival mass with local bone destruction
pathognomonic.notes: Typical location in sacrococcygeal or skull base region
searchTerms: growing mass at base of skull
bone destruction near sacrum or clivus

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cranial nerve palsies due to clival tumor compression
searchTerms: nerve palsies from skull base tumor

common.symptomName: Chronic localized pain at tumor site
Headache associated with skull base involvement
common.notes: Due to increased intracranial pressure or local invasion
searchTerms: painful head due to skull involvement
head pain related to base of skull

common.symptomName: Radiculopathy or nerve root compression symptoms
Dysphagia or dysphonia from cranial nerve involvement

occasional.symptomName: Urinary or bowel incontinence from sacral nerve compression
occasional.notes: Due to involvement of sacral nerve roots
searchTerms: loss of bladder or bowel control

occasional.symptomName: Visual disturbances from optic pathway compression
searchTerms: blurred vision from optic nerve pressure
vision problems due to optic pathway compression
loss of visual field from nerve compression

occasional.symptomName: Hearing loss from cranial nerve VIII involvement
occasional.notes: Rare but reported in skull base tumors
searchTerms: difficulty hearing due to cranial nerve involvement

occasional.symptomName: Neck stiffness or limited range of motion

rare.symptomName: Hydrocephalus secondary to tumor obstruction of CSF pathways
searchTerms: fluid buildup in brain from blocked CSF
brain swelling due to tumor blocking fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor obstruction
back pain with nerve compression signs
weakness or numbness from spinal cord squeezing

rare.symptomName: Systemic constitutional symptoms such as weight loss

laboratory: No specific blood markers; routine labs usually normal
imaging: MRI showing lobulated, destructive midline bone tumor with soft tissue mass
CT demonstrating bone destruction in sacrum or clivus
Characteristic T2 hyperintensity and heterogeneous enhancement on MRI
other: Histopathology showing physaliphorous cells with vacuolated cytoplasm
Immunohistochemistry positive for brachyury, cytokeratin, and S100

distinguishingFeatures: Typically lateral bone involvement rather than midline
Different histological appearance without physaliphorous cells
Lack of physaliphorous cells and brachyury positivity

redFlags: Severe localized bone pain with palpable mass
references: Chugh R, et al. Chordoma: the nonsarcoma primary bone tumor. Oncologist. 2007;12(11):1344-1350.
